purpose: Compare complete named states after the modern tax-zero solve, isolate numerically weak pseudo-zero phases, and test whether removing those degrees of numerical freedom restores the published M5/Bakken carbon-tax continuation.

named_state_comparison.reference: archived tax-zero optimum reconstructed in the modern model
named_state_comparison.candidate: fresh modern tax-zero optimum with exact historical NL column order
named_state_comparison.interpretation: The initial all-variable comparison was confounded by inactive variables and serializer fixed-status differences. Restricting by the exported active NL map leaves 68 material differences. Sixty-six are compositions in four pseudo-zero phases whose component flows are each initialized near 1e-8 mol/s. Their normalization equations therefore have coefficients near 1e-7, allowing compositions to drift from normalized archived fractions toward approximately 0.998 without exceeding the global feasibility tolerance. This is a real degeneracy, but the remaining active state also contains many small differences, especially in R102.

regularization.method: For the four explicitly guarded pseudo-zero inlet phases only, verify total phase flow below 1e-6 mol/s, fix phase compositions to normalized starting component flows, and deactivate the corresponding flow-normalization equations.
regularization.scope: Opt-in diagnostic only; it is not enabled by the default reproduction command.

experiments.path: archived USD 0.01/tonne optimum directly to USD 1/tonne with pseudo-zero regularization
experiments.classification: Accepted alternate local optimum; removing the pseudo-zero degeneracy does not recover the publication branch.

experiments.path: archived USD 0.01/tonne optimum to USD 0.02/tonne with pseudo-zero regularization
experiments.classification: Even a twofold tax step crosses a high-quality iterate and then leaves the basin during strict convergence; step size alone is not the root cause.

experiments.path: same USD 0.02/tonne step with bounded acceptable termination
experiments.classification: Numerically bounded engineering point, not a strict reproduction result. An earlier screen that set only IPOPT acceptable_tol was rejected because IPOPT accepted a scaled aggregate error while unscaled dual infeasibility remained 36.3.

experiments.path: bounded geometric continuation from USD 0.02 to 0.05/tonne
experiments.classification: Second bounded point remained in the intended basin after restoration.

experiments.path: bounded geometric continuation from USD 0.05 to 0.10/tonne
experiments.classification: Failed and left the basin; the remaining requested continuation points were intentionally not run from the invalid state.

commands.active_state_comparison: conda run --no-capture-output -n cistar-idaes-2.12 python reproducibility/compare_named_states.py ARCHIVED_STATE.json FRESH_STATE.json --active-variable-map CANDIDATE_A1_SYMBOL_MAP.json --output COMPARISON.json
commands.strict_small_step: conda run --no-capture-output -n cistar-idaes-2.12 python reproducibility/run_m5_bakken_tax_series.py --ipopt IPOPT --linear-solver ma27 --initial-optimal-tax 0.00001 --tax-rates 0.00002 --max-iter 100 --file-determinism sort-symbols --column-order-from-symbol-map CANDIDATE_A1_SYMBOL_MAP.json --regularize-pseudo-zero-inlet-phases --output RESULT.json
commands.bounded_screen: conda run --no-capture-output -n cistar-idaes-2.12 python reproducibility/run_m5_bakken_tax_series.py --ipopt IPOPT --linear-solver ma27 --initial-optimal-tax 0.00001 --tax-rates 0.00002 0.00005 0.0001 --max-iter 100 --file-determinism sort-symbols --column-order-from-symbol-map CANDIDATE_A1_SYMBOL_MAP.json --regularize-pseudo-zero-inlet-phases --acceptable-tol 0.01 --acceptable-iter 1 --output RESULT.json

conclusions: Name-aligned active-state comparison identifies four structurally absent inlet phases as the dominant state drift after a fresh modern tax-zero solve.
Guarded elimination of the 66 weak normalization equations reduces a genuine degeneracy but does not by itself restore strict continuation convergence or prevent an alternate local optimum.
A much smaller tax increment still crosses a nearly feasible and nearly stationary point before restoration failure, rejecting large continuation step size as the sole cause.
Explicitly bounded acceptable termination can retain two early engineering points, but it fails at USD 0.10/tonne and is not accepted as the Phase B reproduction policy.
The remaining obstruction is strict, representation-robust KKT convergence in the residual active state, with R102 derivative/heat variables the largest absolute checkpoint differences.
